==English== {{wp|+ship}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|frind||pronunciation spelling}} * {{alt|en|freind||misspelling}} ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:frend|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|freend}}, {{m|enm|frend}}, {{m|enm|frende}}, {{m|enm|freynde}}, {{m|enm|friend}}, {{m|enm|frind}}, {{m|enm|frond}}, {{m|enm|frund}}, {{m|enm|vrend}}, {{m|enm|vryend}}, from {{inh|en|ang|frēond}}, {{m|ang|frīond|t=friend|lit=loving [one], lover}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*friund}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*frijōndz|t=friend, loved one}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*preyH-|t=to please; to love}}, roughly equivalent to {{suffix|enm|free|and|alt2=nd|nocat=1}}. See also [[Friday]]. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|sco|freend|t=friend}}, {{cog|yol|friend}}, {{m|yol|vriene|t=friend}}, {{cog|frr|frinj}}, {{m|frr|frün|t=friend}}, {{cog|stq|Fjund}}, {{m|stq|Früünd|t=friend}}, {{cog|fy|freon}}, {{m|fy|freondinne|t=friend}}, {{cog|cim|bròint}}, {{m|cim|vròint|t=friend}}, {{cog|nl|vriend|t=friend}}, {{cog|de|Freund|t=friend}}, {{cog|nds-de|Fründ|t=friend, relative}}, {{cog|li|vröndj|t=friend}}, {{cog|lb|Frënd|t=friend}}, {{cog|wym|fraeind}}, {{m|wym|frajnd|t=friend}}, {{cog|yi|פֿרײַנד|t=friend}}, {{cog|da|frænde|t=kinsman}}, {{cog|fo,is|frændi|t=kinsman}}, {{cog|nb,nn|frende|t=relative}}, {{cog|sv|frände|t=kinsman, relative}}, {{cog|got|𐍆𐍂𐌹𐌾𐍉𐌽𐌳𐍃|t=friend}}; also {{cog|cy|rhydd|t=free}}, {{cog|la|proprius|t=own, proper}}, {{cog|be|пры́яцель|t=friend}}, {{cog|bg|прия́тел|t=male friend}}, {{cog|cs|přítel|t=friend; supporter; lover}}, {{cog|mk|при́јател|t=friend, mate, pal}}, {{cog|pl|przyjaciel}}, {{m|pl|przyjáciel|t=friend; lover}}, {{cog|ru|прия́тель|t=friend; buddy, mate, pal}}, {{cog|sh|при̏јатељ}}, {{m|sh|prȉjatelj|t=friend}}, {{cog|sk|priateľ|t=friend; supporter}}, {{cog|sl|prijatelj|t=friend; companion; chum}}, {{cog|uk|при́ятель|t=friend; buddy, pal}}, {{cog|ae|𐬟𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬀|t=good, pleasant}}, {{cog|fa|فری|tr=fari|t=beloved, dear; pleasing}}, {{cog|sa|प्रिय|t=beloved; own, wonted}}. More at {{m|en|free}}. {{col-bottom}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|frĕnd|a=RP,GA}}, {{IPA|en|/fɹɛnd/|[fɹ̥ɛnd]|[fɹ̥ɛnd̥]}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-friend.ogg|a=RP}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-friend.ogg|a=GA}} * {{IPA|en|/frɪnd/|a=dialectal,especially with <>|ref={{R:Bingham IP|75}}}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛnd|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|friend}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # A person, typically someone other than a [[family]] [[member]], [[spouse]] or [[lover]], whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels [[affection]]. #* {{RQ:Austen Emma|passage="[…]if you have any wish to speak openly to me as a '''friend''', or to ask my opinion of any thing that you may have in contemplation—as a '''friend''', indeed, you may command me.—I will hear whatever you like. I will tell you exactly what I think." "As a '''friend'''!"—repeated Mr. Knightley.—"Emma, that I fear is a word—No, I have no wish—[…]”}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1841|author=w:Ralph Waldo Emerson|chapter=Friendship|title={{w|Essays: First Series|Essays}}|volume=I |passage=The only reward of virtue is virtue; the only way to have a '''friend''' is to be one.}} #* '''1917''', Richard M. Gummere translating {{w|Seneca the Younger|Seneca}} as ''{{w|Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium|Ad Lucilium Epistulae Morales}}'', Loeb Classical Library, Vol. I, [[:s:Moral letters to Lucilius/Letter 3|No. 3]]: #* '''1923''', William Armistead Falconer translating {{w|Cicero}} as ''[https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Cicero/Laelius_de_Amicitia/text*.html De Amicitia]'', Loeb Classical Library, Vol. XX, p. 34: #* '''1927 Mar. 31''', {{w|Ernest Hemingway}}, [https://books.google.com.hk/books?id=SgKeQfmimJEC&pg=PA248 letter] to {{w|F. Scott Fitzgerald}}: #*: ...you are my devoted '''friend''' too. You do more and work harder and oh shit I'd get [[maudlin]] about how damned [[swell]] you are. My god I'd like to see you... You're a hell of a good guy. #* '''1933 Dec. 12''', {{w|Walter Winchell}}, "On Broadway", ''Scranton Republican'', p. 5: #: {{ux|en|John and I have been '''friends''' ever since we were roommates at college.}} #: {{ux|en|Trust is important between '''friends'''.}} #: {{ux|en|I used to find it hard to make '''friends''' when I was shy.}} #: {{ux|en|We became '''friends''' in the war and remain '''friends''' to this day.}} #: {{ux|en|We were '''friends''' with some girls from the other school and stayed '''friends''' with them.}} # An [[associate]] who provides [[assistance]]; patron, mentor. #* {{quote-book|en|format=letter|year=1779|author={{w|Benjamin Franklin}}|title=[[s:The Whistle (Franklin, 1779)|The Whistle]]|text=When I was a child of seven years old, my '''friends''', on a holiday, filled my little pocket with halfpence.}} #* {{RQ:Austen Pride and Prejudice|text= The vicious propensities—the want of principle which he was careful to guard from the knowledge of his best '''friend''', could not escape the observation of a young man of nearly the same age with himself, and who had opportunities of seeing him in unguarded moments, which Mr. Darcy could not have.}} #* {{quote-book|en|format=poem|year=1907|author={{w|Hilaire Belloc}}|title=[[s:Cautionary Tales for Children/Jim|Jim]]|text= There was a Boy whose name was Jim; His '''Friends''' were very good to him. They gave him Tea, and Cakes, and Jam, And slices of delicious Ham, And Chocolate with pink inside, And little Tricycles to ride, And read him Stories through and through, And even took him to the Zoo—}} #: {{ux|en|The Automobile Association is every motorist's '''friend'''.   The police is every law-abiding citizen's '''friend'''.}} # A person with whom one is [[vaguely]] or [[indirectly]] [[acquainted]]. #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman |volume=189|issue=2|page=27|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google The tao of tech] |passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you "stay up to date with what your '''friends''' are doing",{{...}}and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.}} #: {{coi|en|a '''friend''' of a '''friend'''}} #: {{ux|en|I added him as a '''friend''' on Facebook, but I hardly know him.}} # A person who backs or supports something. #: {{ux|en|I’m not a '''friend''' of cheap wine.}} # {{lb|en|informal}} An object or idea that can be used for good. #: {{ux|en|Fruit is your '''friend'''.}} # {{lb|en|colloquial|ironic|used only in the [[vocative]]}} {{n-g|Used as a form of [[address]] when [[warn]]ing someone.}} #: {{ux|en|You’d better watch it, '''friend'''.}} # {{lb|en|object-oriented programming}} A [[function]] or [[class]] granted special access to the [[private]] and [[protected]] [[member]]s of another class. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=D S Malik|title=C++ Programming: From Problem Analysis to Program Design|passage=To make a function be a '''friend''' to a class, the reserved word friend precedes the function prototype{{...}}}} # {{lb|en|climbing}} A [[spring-loaded camming device]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1995|title=Rock Climbing Basics |passage=Since they were introduced in the 1970s, '''friends''' have revolutionized climbing, making protection possible in previously impossible places {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|euphemistic}} A [[lover]]; a [[boyfriend]] or [[girlfriend]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Love's Labour's Lost|5|2|passage=Nor to the motion of a schoolboy's tongue ; Nor never come in visard to my '''friend'''}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1813|author=Samuel Foote|title=The Commissary, Etc.|page=17 |passage=Time has been, when a gentleman wanted a '''friend''', I could supply him with choice in an hour; but the market is spoiled, and a body might as soon produce a hare or a partridge {{...}}}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=1975|author=w:Janis Ian|title=In the Winter |passage=I met your '''friend'''. She's very nice, what can I say?}} # {{lb|en|Scotland|obsolete}} A [[relative]], a [[relation]] by blood or marriage. #: '''''Friends''' agree best at a distance.'' #: ''Make '''friends''' of framet folk.'' # {{lb|en|in the plural|usually preceded by "and"}} {{ng|Used to refer collectively to a group of associated individuals, especially those comprising a cast, company, or crew}} #: {{syn|en|company|alt1=and company|et al.}} #: {{ux|en|Meanwhile on ''The View'', Whoopi Goldberg and '''friends''' continue to spout their takes on the hot topics of the day.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2020|author=Beth Van Schaack|title=Imagining Justice for Syria|isbn=9780190055967|page=98 |text=Russia and '''friends''' continued to criticize the work of the JIM, focusing in particular on the methodology employed and the decision of the experts not to go to certain on-site visits for security reasons{{nb...}}}} ====Usage notes==== * ''friends'' is found as an invariable plural in the phrases ''make friends with'' and ''be friends with'': ''I am '''friends''' with her''; ''He made '''friends''' with his co-worker.'' * We usually ''[[make]] a friend'', or ''make friends with'' someone. See '''[[:Appendix:Collocations of do, have, make, and take]]''' * In older texts and certain dialects, the prepositional phrase '''to friend''' means "as a friend or an ally", for exampleː "[https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Faerie_Queene/Book_I/Canto_I with God to frend] (Spenser)". The antonym to the phrase '''to friend''' is '''to [[fiend]]'''. ====Synonyms==== * {{sense|person one likes to socialize with}} {{see thesaurus|en|friend}} * {{sense|sympathizer, helper}} as a friend to, to [[befriend]]; to be friendly to, to help. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1596|author=Edmund Spenser|title=The Faerie Queene|section=IV.ii |passage=Lo sluggish Knight the victors happie pray: / So fortune '''friends''' the bold [...].}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1896|author=w:Alfred Edward Housman|title=w:A Shropshire Lad|section=LXII |passage=’Tis true, the stuff I bring for sale
Is not so brisk a brew as ale:
Out of a stem that scored the hand
I wrung it in a weary land.
But take it: if the smack is sour,
The better for the embittered hour;
It should do good to heart and head
When your soul is in my soul’s stead;
And I will '''friend''' you, if I may,
In the dark and cloudy day.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To add (a person) to a [[list]] of friends on a [[social networking]] site; to officially designate (someone) as a friend. #: {{ant|en|defriend|unfriend}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Kevin Farnham; Dale G. Farnham|title=Myspace Safety: 51 Tips for Teens And Parents|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=t0ykIJl4oAEC&pg=PA69&dq=%22friend+someone%22&sig=ACfU3U07tfwMQUkPDjT1RSxhAX6wgSJG6w|page=69|publisher=How-To Primers|isbn=0977883353 |passage=One of the most used features of MySpace is the practice that is nicknamed "friending." If you "'''friend'''" someone, then that person is added to your MySpace friends list, and you are added to their friends list.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=David Fono; Kate Raynes-Goldie|chapter=Hyperfriendship and Beyond: Friends and Social Norms on LiveJournal|editor=Mia Consalvo; Caroline Haythornthwaite|title=Internet Research Annual: Selected Papers from the Association of Internet Researchers Conference 2005|volume=4|series=Digital Formations|seriesvolume=33|location=New York, N.Y.|publisher=w:[[Peter Lang (publisher)|Peter Lang]]|issn=1526-3169|isbn=9780820478579|page=99|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=I0sKFgXY9D4C&pg=PA99&dq=friend|passage=The two distributions which exhibited this property were in response to the statements, “I am careful about who I '''friend''',” and, “If someone friends me, I will '''friend''' them.” (Figure 3).}} ====Translations==== {{trans-see|befriend}} {{trans-top|to act as the friend of}} * Afrikaans: * Belarusian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * German: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|дружи́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|подружи́ться|pf}} * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tatar: * Zazaki: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to add as a friend}} * Afrikaans: * Bulgarian: * Chinese: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * Hungarian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|зафре́ндить|pf|tr=zafrɛńditʹ}} {{qualifier|Internet}}, {{t|ru|[[доба́вить]] в [[друзья́]]}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Slovak: * Spanish: * Tagalog: * Ukrainian: * Zazaki: {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== {{reflist}} ===Further reading=== * {{R:OneLook}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=definr|Friden|finder|frined|redfin|refin'd|refind}} {{cln|en|endearing terms|terms of address}} {{C|en|People|Friendship}}
